statement: The ideals of R_0 are {0} and J u {0} for the ideals J of R; its prime ideals are eta = {0} and P u {0}, P in Spec R (R a nonzero commutative ring).

Every point of Spec R_0 lies in the closure of eta; {eta} is open and its complement V(0^) is homeomorphic to Spec R; the open sets are the empty set and {eta} u U with U open in Spec R; the localization at eta is the Boolean semifield B; if dim R is finite, dim R_0 = dim R + 1.

The congruences of R_0 are two for each ideal J of R, both restricting to congruence modulo J on R: in the first, 0 lies in the class of 0^ and the quotient is R/J; in the second, 0 is alone in its class and the quotient is (R/J)_0 (B for J = R).

For an R_0-semimodule M put eps(m) = 0^m, L_M = 0^M, M_l = eps^-1(l). L_M is the set of additive idempotents, a join-semilattice with least element 0_M; each M_l is an R-module with zero l; with T_{l,l'}(m) = m + l', (L_M, (M_l), (T_{l,l'})) is a strong semilattice of R-modules and m + n = T(m) + T(n) in the fibre over eps(m) + eps(n). This is an equivalence from R_0-semimodules to strong semilattices of R-modules, under which the cancellative semimodules correspond to the R-modules.

A finitely generated R_0-semimodule is projective iff it is isomorphic to some P(J, Q): J a finite poset, Q_j finitely generated projective R-modules, the strong semilattice over Idl(J) with fibre the direct sum of the Q_j over U. The semilattices of idempotents of the finitely generated projective R_0-semimodules are exactly the finite distributive lattices.

Every commutative inverse monoid has exactly one structure of Z_0-semimodule, and the category of Z_0-semimodules is isomorphic to that of commutative inverse monoids; a finitely generated commutative inverse monoid is projective iff it is isomorphic to P(J, (Z^{n_j})) for a finite poset J and integers n_j >= 0.

p: R_0 -> R (the identity on R, p(0) = 0^) and chi: R_0 -> B (R to 1, 0 to 0) are surjective homomorphisms of semirings, and (p, chi): R_0 -> R x B is injective with image {(x, b): b = 0 implies x = 0^}.

For R = F_2 the ideals of R_0 = {0, 0^, 1} are {0} c {0, 0^} c R_0, the first two prime, and there are four congruences, with quotients (F_2)_0, F_2, B and the zero semiring; for R = Z the spectrum is the chain eta, then {0, 0^}, then pZ u {0}, of dimension 2.

For commutative rings R and S, (R x S)_0 is isomorphic to the fibre product R_0 x_B S_0 over the two support maps; Spec (R x S)_0 is the disjoint union of Spec R and Spec S with one generic point common to both.

For the ring of integers O_K of a number field, the finite quotients of (O_K)_0 of the first kind are the rings O_K/J, counted by sum N(J)^-s = zeta_K(s), those of the second kind have N(J) + 1 elements; for R = Z, counting all finite quotient semirings of Z_0 by their number of elements gives sum n^-s + sum (n+1)^-s = 2 zeta(s) - 1.

R_0 has the idempotents 0 < 0^ and the fibres {0} and R; an R-module through p is one fibre; B through chi has two idempotents and two zero fibres; R_0^n has the Boolean lattice of subsets of {1..n} as its semilattice, with fibre R^S over S.
The semilattice L_M is a B-module regarded as an R_0-semimodule through chi, and eps: M -> L_M is the universal homomorphism from M to a B-module.
A finite join-semilattice with least element is a retract of a finite Boolean lattice P({1..n}), by maps preserving joins and the least element, iff it is a distributive lattice.
For J = {a < b} and Q_a = Q_b = R, P(J, Q) = {(0,0)} u (R x {0}) u (R x R) in R_0^2 is projective, not free, and not an R-module; the smallest projective with a zero module is B = P({a}, 0).

If M is isomorphic to P(J, Q), then J is isomorphic to the poset of join-irreducible elements of L_M, and Q_j to M_{down j}/T(M_{down j minus j}); so isomorphism classes of finitely generated projective R_0-semimodules correspond to isomorphism classes of finite posets with a finitely generated projective R-module at each element.

The R-modules are the semimodules with one idempotent, and none of them but 0 is projective over R_0 (a section into a free semimodule is zero, as free semimodules are zerosumfree); projective R-modules occur instead as fibres over 0^. Supersedes two sentences of the draft (section 1.3 and this remark) that said the projective semimodules with one idempotent are the projective R-modules.
R_0 is zerosumfree, has no zero divisors, and every ideal of R_0 is subtractive (R any commutative ring).
For commutative rings R and S, g -> g_0 is a bijection from the ring homomorphisms R -> S to the semiring homomorphisms R_0 -> S_0; in particular Aut R_0 = Aut R.

The units of R act on R_0 by additive automorphisms; with I the ideal generated by the u - 1 (u a unit), the common fixed points are Ann_R(I) u {0}; they are exactly the two zeros iff Ann_R(I) = {0^} (for instance a domain with a unit u != 1, every ring of integers, every field other than F_2); {0, 0^} is closed under both operations and isomorphic to B.

For the zero ring, (0)_0 = {0^, 0} with 0^ = 1 is B; the support map R_0 -> B is the image of R -> 0 and the only homomorphism R_0 -> B; adjoining a zero to the chain L_n gives L_{n+1}, so from B = L_2 adjoining zeros gives all finite chains.
